The learned Subordinate Judge considering the case on merit held that plaintiff proved the contract for sale in respect of Schedule-1 and Schedule-2 properties and Also proved the payment of Tk. 3,000/- and Tk. 2,000/- to defendant No. 1 and the construction of 2 huts on second schedule property and decreed the suit against the defendant No. 1 and exparte against defendant No. 2. 

 6. Mr. M.H. Khandker, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the appellant has urged that Mr. Md. Sheikh Sadeq, Additional District Judge, 4th Court, Mymensingh who dismissed the appeal confirming the judgment and decree of the trial court was previously Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Mymensingh and dealt with the suit for about 2 years when it was fixed for pre-emptory hearing but was not heard; further, Mr. Sadeq was Munsif, 2nd Court, Mymensingh, when the plaintiff was his Sheristader, and that these facts were not known to him when Mr. Sadeq as Additional District Judge heard the appeal and as such he did not raise any objection at that time. The learned Single Judge of the High Court Division before whom the objection was raised for the first time was of the view that the plaintiff might have been Sheristadar of the Court of 2nd Munsif when Mr. Sadeq had been Munsif of that court, but for that reason it cannot be said that Mr. Sadeq after being appointed as Additional District Judge should not have heard the appeal. If, however, defendant No. 1 was under any impression that he would not get justice before him for the aforesaid reasons he should have filed an application before the learned District Judge for transfer Of the appeal to some other court. But that was not done. According to him, defendant No.1 did not apprehend any prejudice at that stage if the appeal was heard by Mr. Sadeq and in that view of the matter the objection is not tenable.
